_comment: SIXTY ITERATIONS IS A SEARCH BUDGET, AND THE BUTTON WAS PAYING IT.
The user's live seed-16 game, turn 4 main ordinal 61 -- a state they said plainly should
always win. Emiel the Blessed and Cloud of Faeries on the battlefield; Adarkar Wastes
carrying BOTH Fertile Ground and Trace of Abundance (so the board makes any colour);
Brushland, Kitchen (the {4},{T} Investigate draw land) and Yavimaya Coast. Cloud untaps
TWO, the best two are worth 4, Emiel blinks for {3}: net **+1** a pass. A card costs SIX
(Kitchen's {4} plus the Clue's {2}). The Living Wish is roughly twenty cards down a
46-card library.
So the dig alone wants ~120 iterations and `FlickerMaxIterations` is 60. The rule fired
WISH-DRAW, correctly -- the arithmetic really does fund the path -- and the click failed
twice, because the loop stopped half way down the dig. Measured on the live frame:
MTG_COMBO_OFF_MAX_ITER=60 -> 'blink Cloud of Faeries x60 -- COMBO OFF (NOT PROVEN)';
default 400 -> 'blink Cloud of Faeries x210 -- COMBO OFF: wins this turn', VERIFIED.
Nothing was broken but the budget.
The ceiling could not simply be raised: `FlickerMaxIterations` also sizes
`FlickerGoOffCount` for the SEARCH (BlinkActivationCounts, EdfAutoGoOffAfterCasts), so a
global raise re-prices every autonomous go-off and moves ground truth, the value leaf and
the keep tables. `FlickerIterationCeiling` is HumanPlayActive()-gated instead, and every
consumer reads it together -- the count sizer, the exact (mana, pips) bank, and the cheap
lethal projection that decides whether a trial apply is paid for at all. A bank sized at
400 behind a projection still bounded at 60 would show a button it could never verify.
ITS OWN NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the discrimination is exact at every dig depth:
CO_ENV='MTG_COMBO_OFF_MAX_ITER=60' bash test/combo_off_check.sh   -> this one FAILS
wish depth   5  10  15  20  25  30
ceiling 400  x81 x117 x162 x207 x252 x297  -- all VERIFIED
ceiling  60  x60 x60  x60  x60  x60  x60   -- none offered as proven
Cost, measured paired on the user's own line (66 frames, 56 trial applies, identical
picks): 0.29 ms per trial at 60 -> 0.81 ms per trial at 400. A trial that fails is rolled
back whole (MTG_COMBO_OFF_ROLLBACK), so an over-large ceiling costs time and nothing else.
Reconstruction caveat: the live frame carried {G:17 C:2} floating, which a --scenario
fixture cannot stage, so this board is strictly harder than the one the user sat in front
of -- and it still wins.
